title: The Asset of the DMZ
premise: Jude Okonkwo, a disgraced intelligence analyst with three agencies on her termination list, is living off-grid in a Panmunjom-adjacent safe house when a real estate listing surfaces online — complete with interior photos of her hiding place, down to the false wall. The listing is a message: someone knows where she is, and they want her to run. Instead she runs toward it, uncovering a defector — North Korean cryptographer Min-jun Seo — whose 'rescue' was engineered as bait to flush out a mole inside the joint command. As Jude and Min-jun flee south through the DMZ's kill zones, she discovers the mole is the mentor who burned her career, and that her own termination was cover for making her deniable. In the end, Jude chooses justice over reinstatement, exposing the mole via a live broadcast from the truce village, and chooses belonging over duty, walking away with Min-jun rather than handing him to any flag.
about_author: Isandro Okonkwo is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian convoys who spent a decade along contested borders before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people the system discards, drawing on the border towns where he learned that loyalty is a currency and everyone's exchange rate is different.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Scrolling property listings at 3 a.m., she freezes on a photo of a safe house — her safe house — staged with her own go-bag visible on the bed. The emotional beat is cold dread: her invisibility, the one thing she had left, has been sold to the highest bidder.

chapters.title: Three Strikes
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Jude's POV tracing her terminations from three agencies, each dismissal stranger and less explained than the last. She rehearses her polished lie — 'I ask too many questions' — while packing. Beat: weary self-awareness masking fear that the lie is wrong.

chapters.title: The Man in the Listing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She zooms into a photo and spots a reflection in a window: a man holding the camera, wearing an old joint-command lanyard. She recognizes the lanyard before the face. Beat: the past she fled has found her address.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Reverse
chapters.summary: POV shift to Colonel Ada Reyes, the mentor who once championed Jude, now chairing a quiet meeting about 'Asset DMZ-7' — a defector extraction that needs a deniable, disposable analyst. Reyes suggests a name. Beat: chilling bureaucratic betrayal dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Call She Shouldn't Take
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. An untraceable call offers her reinstatement in exchange for one extraction: Min-jun Seo, a North Korean cryptographer waiting at a forward post. She knows it's bait. She says yes anyway. Beat: reckless hope — the first thing she's wanted in years.

chapters.title: Min-jun
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV. Waiting in a drainage tunnel beneath the western corridor, he reviews the coded instructions he himself helped design — and realizes the extraction route is a kill box. He goes anyway, carrying a drive that could topple careers in two capitals. Beat: terrified resolve.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, night crossing. She meets Min-jun at the tunnel mouth; he tests her with a challenge phrase she wasn't given, and she answers it correctly by instinct — from a briefing she was never supposed to remember. Beat: mutual suspicion sharpening into grudging respect.

chapters.title: The Kill Box Closes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Flares ignite the corridor as a strike team — not theirs — hits the extraction point. Jude improvises a route through a minefield using a survey map only she ever flagged as misprinted. Beat: adrenaline-fueled competence, her first taste of being needed.

chapters.title: What He Carries
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV, hiding in a pump house. He explains the drive: decryption keys proving a joint cyber-operation was deliberately aimed at civilian infrastructure — and that the order came from inside. Beat: the weight of witness, and his fear that no one wants the truth.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They hole up in a fisherman's cottage she'd pre-stocked years ago — a paranoia habit that finally pays off. She realizes the cottage's location was in her sealed personnel file. Someone is reading her file in real time. Beat: the hunted becoming hunters.

chapters.title: Reyes's Ledger
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. She reviews the operation and discovers someone above her is feeding the hunters Jude's locations — and that her own name is next on the cleanup list. Beat: the architect realizing she built her own trap.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Dusk
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A smuggler named Hana agrees to move them down the coast, but only after recognizing Jude from an old wanted bulletin. The price: the drive's location. Beat: negotiation as intimacy — two women who trust nothing, trading anyway.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Kindness
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV. Aboard the ferry, Jude shares her food and her real name — the first time in years. Min-jun, trained to expect cruelty, is undone by ordinary decency. Beat: the first fragile thread of love, spun from shared exile.

chapters.title: The Mole's Signature
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, decrypting en route. The leak pattern in her terminations and the DMZ operation matches one handler's style — the man who trained her, Director Elias Voss. Beat: betrayal recontextualizing her whole life; every failure was authored.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A surprise inspection at a river checkpoint; Min-jun poses as a repatriation case while Jude talks her way past a young officer who idolizes the agencies that discarded her. Beat: the irony of the system's faithful protecting its castoffs.

chapters.title: Hana's Price Comes Due
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Hana sells their route to Voss's hunters — then, hearing what the drive contains, sells the hunters a false route instead, choosing a side for the first time in her life. Beat: redemption purchased cheap and paid for dear.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV. The false route still catches them at the flats. A hunter — a former colleague of Jude's — has Min-jun dead to rights until Jude walks into the open as a distraction, bleeding. Beat: love made visible as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Field Surgery
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, half-lucid. Min-jun, whose hands were built for keyboards, extracts shrapnel from her side using ferry first-aid and her own shouted instructions. Beat: vulnerability exchanged like vows; duty dissolving into devotion.

chapters.title: Reyes Defects From Herself
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. She burns her own career to send Jude the one thing she needs: Voss's travel schedule and the location of the second safe house — the real one. Beat: a mentor's apology delivered as tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Second Safe House
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach the true safe house, and inside find evidence Voss staged the entire listing, the extraction, the kill box — a machine built to destroy the drive and everyone who touched it. Beat: clarity and fury; the game board finally visible.

chapters.title: What Min-jun Saw
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV, a long flashback to the North: the strike orders he decrypted, the village, the silence afterward. He explains why he defected — not for freedom, but because someone had to remember. Beat: grief as the engine of courage.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Voss calls the safe house landline directly. He offers her everything back — rank, clearance, her name cleared — if she delivers Min-jun and the drive. Beat: temptation laid bare; the life she mourned, priced at one man.

chapters.title: The Answer Is the Silence
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV. He hears her hesitate, and waits. Jude hangs up without answering, then tells Min-jun the truth about her three terminations and the lie she'd polished. Beat: honesty as the foundation stone of love against duty.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Door
chapters.summary: Dual POV, siege chapter. Voss's team hits the safe house; Jude and Min-jun escape through the false wall from the listing photo — the architecture of her exposure becoming her salvation. Beat: the past weaponized, then turned.

chapters.title: The Truce Village
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They run for the Joint Security Area, where cameras never blink and a live feed never cuts. Her plan: justice outside the law requires the one courtroom no agency controls — public witness. Beat: audacious hope with a body count if it fails.

chapters.title: Reyes's Last Order
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. She orders her remaining loyalists to stand down and personally clears the corridor to the JSA, knowing she'll be arrested by morning. Beat: a soldier choosing conscience over command for the first time.

chapters.title: The Blue Bridge
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV. Crossing the Bridge of No Return in reverse — toward the cameras, toward the South's side of the line — he recites the names from his village. Beat: pilgrimage; the defector walking toward judgment of his own design.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, the only chapter from the antagonist. He enters the JSA under diplomatic cover, certain the drive is a bluff and Jude is broken goods. Beat: arrogance meeting its accounting; the reader sees his certainty begin to crack.

chapters.title: Live
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax begins. In front of press pooled at the truce village, she plugs the drive into a broadcast laptop and narrates the decryption live — the strike orders, the civilian coordinates, the authorizing signature. Beat: controlled fury as testimony.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Dual POV, climax peak. The final decrypted page displays Voss's authorization code. He moves to seize the drive; Min-jun steps between him and the laptop, and Reyes — in cuffs — confirms the code's provenance on camera. Beat: the mole unmasked by the people he discarded.

chapters.title: Arrest on Camera
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Military police, unable to ignore a global broadcast, take Voss into custody as he reaches for a diplomatic exit that no longer exists. Beat: justice outside the law, enforced by the law's own embarrassment.

chapters.title: The Debrief They Wanted
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Agencies descend offering reinstatement, book deals, silence agreements. She listens to all of it, holding Min-jun's hand under the table. Beat: the old hunger for belonging-to-an-institution meeting a new belonging-to-a-person.

chapters.title: Min-jun's Choice
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV. He's offered asylum, a lab, a life of quiet importance — contingent on distance from the scandal-touched Jude. Beat: he discovers that duty can be a cage in any country, and refuses the cage.

chapters.title: Reyes's Sentence
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV, brief. Facing court-martial, she refuses counsel and uses her testimony to bury Voss deeper. She sends Jude one line: 'You were never the problem. You were the proof.' Beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years — then repacks it, lighter, deliberately. She isn't running anymore; she just likes knowing the door is hers. Beat: trauma metabolized into freedom.

chapters.title: Hana's Harbor
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The smuggler offers them passage anywhere; they choose a fishing town where nobody asks questions and everyone knows everyone. Beat: belonging found in the unlikeliest registry — a community of people off all books.

chapters.title: The Drive, Distributed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She mirrors the drive to a thousand dead-drops and journalists before surrendering the original, ensuring no court, agency, or fire can bury it. Beat: justice made permanent by redundancy.

chapters.title: What the Village Remembers
chapters.summary: Min-jun's POV. He builds a small memorial for his village on the harbor's edge, and Jude stands with him through the whole night vigil. Beat: grief shared becomes grief halved; love stated without declaration.

chapters.title: The Listing, Deleted
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She finds the real estate listing finally taken down, the photos gone. On a whim she lists the cottage in town — honestly, her own name attached, her face in the photos. Beat: the woman who hid everywhere chooses to be findable.

chapters.title: Asset No More
chapters.summary: Dual POV, closing chapter. A year later: Min-jun teaching, Jude consulting only on her own terms, a letter from Reyes arriving postmarked from a prison library. On the porch, watching the boats, they agree the best intelligence is knowing what you won't trade. Beat: quiet, earned peace — belonging, love, and justice all kept.
